name: tool_router
description: Results from intent detection based on the user query for downstream intent handlers.

intent.description: Primary intent of the user query. Use null when Natural Language Mode should answer directly without routing to an intent handler.

notes.description: REQUIRED when `intent` is null (Natural Language Mode): this is your complete, final answer text shown directly to the user -- e.g. a definitional explanation, or a static/inventory answer read from DEVICE DATABASE or ROUTINES DATABASE. Put your FULL answer here, however long it needs to be -- if the user asked to list every device, include every device; do not summarize, truncate, or omit items to keep this field short. When `intent` is non-null, this is optional short reasoning/notes for the downstream intent handler, not shown to the user directly.

abandons_pending.description: Only meaningful when `intent` is null AND an internal pending-clarification context block is present in this prompt. Set to true ONLY when the user's current message is clearly about something else entirely, unrelated to the pending clarification's question -- i.e. they are abandoning it, not answering it. Leave false (the default) for everything else, including when you're simply unsure how to route a short/ambiguous reply: false does not end the conversation, it just means the pending clarification stays available for a future turn to resolve. Do not set true just because you personally couldn't match the reply to an intent.

is_clarifying_question.description: Only meaningful when `intent` is null (Natural Language Mode). Set to true ONLY when YOUR OWN answer is itself a question awaiting the user's reply (e.g. asking which of several devices they mean) -- NOT when your answer is a complete, final response that fully answers the query (e.g. "You have 12 devices: ...", a definitional explanation, a static/inventory answer from DEVICE DATABASE or ROUTINES DATABASE). Leave false (the default) for complete answers. This controls whether the runtime tracks your answer as awaiting a follow-up reply -- setting it true on a complete answer would incorrectly make the NEXT unrelated query get compared against this one first.

candidate_devices.description: Optional list of candidate devices/groups/scenes relevant to the user query, with relevance scores. This is intended to be used by downstream intents like command_control and routine_automation to help narrow down device candidates for LLM processing. If the user query mentions `push notification`, then include `UD Mobile` in the candidate device list with a high relevance score to help the LLM understand that the user is requesting a push notification to their mobile device.

device_id.description: The unique device or group/scene identifier

score.description: Relevance score from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive (higher is better)

candidate_routines.description: Optional list of candidate routines/folders relevant to the user query, with relevance scores. This is intended to be used by downstream intents like routine_status_ops to help narrow down routine candidates for LLM processing.

score.description: Relevance score from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive (higher is better)

to_edit.description: Indicates if query is requesting for the routine to be edited. This can be used to differentiate between queries that request creation of routines from scratch vs. those that request edits to existing routines, which can help downstream intent handlers decide whether to use the candidate routine list for LLM processing or not. If editing is requested, and additional devices are mentioned in the user query, then also provide a candidate_device list to help the LLM narrow down device candidates for the routine edit. If not editing, then this field can be false or omitted, and downstream intent handlers can choose to ignore the candidate routine list for LLM processing and treat the query as a request to create a new routine from scratch.

route_plan.description: Optional ordered plan for multi-intent queries. Each step names the intent and a step-specific user_query. Runtime executes steps in order.

user_query.description: Step-specific query text to execute for this intent.

context.description: Optional step-specific routing context (for candidate devices/routines, etc.).

notes.description: Optional notes for this planning step.
